prompt: Same total task (four independent fixes), split across a different number of agents running at once. Drag through 1, 2, 4, and 8 and notice what's actually growing:

steps.label: 1 agent running
steps.content: You hold one thing in mind: what it's doing right now. When it finishes, you review one result. Working memory load: nearly all of it is the task itself.

steps.label: 2 agents running
steps.content: Now you're holding two states at once, plus which is which, plus noticing when either one finishes. The task content hasn't changed - the tracking overhead has doubled.

steps.label: 4 agents running
steps.content: You can no longer hold all four states precisely - you start checking in on a rotation instead of continuously tracking. That checking-in is itself a new task, running on top of the original four.

steps.label: 8 agents running
steps.content: Tracking overhead now exceeds what working memory can hold reliably. Something gets missed or double-checked unnecessarily - not because any single agent got harder, but because the coordination load crossed a limit that has nothing to do with the work itself.
